newsitem.title: FRANCE: France denounces Israeli settlements plan.
newsitem.headline: France denounces Israeli settlements plan.

text.p: France said on Wednesday that an Israeli plan to build 132 housing units for Jews in the heart of Arab East Jerusalem was dangerous for the peace process and could spark new tensions.
"We hope this project will not take effect," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters.
"Such a programme would be dangerous for the peace process as a whole and could lead to new tensions which all parties would suffer from," he said.
Rummelhardt said that it risked jeopardising the demographic make-up of Jerusalem and would thus constitute a new attack on the city's status quo.

The past attack he was apparently referring to was the opening by Israel of an entrance to an archaeological tunnel near Moslem sites in Jerusalem in September, which fuelled a wave of violence in which 60 Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed.
"France calls once again for the respect of the Oslo accords which demand maintaining the status quo pending a negotiated solution for the city," Rummelhardt said.

The future of East Jerusalem, which Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed, is to be determined only in final-status peace talks which have yet to resume under Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who took office in June.
Israel's Jerusalem municipal planning commission approved on Tuesday a plan for Jewish housing in the Ras al-Amoud neighbourhood, where about 11,000 Palestinians live.
